fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Scattered Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflectors on both sides to help responders locate the turnoff quickly, especially at night.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris so responding units can reach the residence without stopping.
• Maintain driveway width wide enough for a fire apparatus or ambulance to pass through without obstruction along the full length.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the residence so large emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim any overhanging branches along the driveway to maintain a clear overhead path for tall emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the driveway edges so responders on foot can move alongside vehicles if needed.
• Post the property address visibly at the residence itself, not only at the road, so responders arriving on scene can confirm they are at the correct structure.
• Mark the location of the detached structure clearly from the driveway so responders can identify all buildings on arrival without searching the property.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can approach and work

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Brush Area; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin trees scattered around the structure to increase open space between the canopy and the building.
• Remove shrubs and brush growing beneath tree canopies near the house to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the trees.
• Clear brush and shrubs along both sides of the driveway to keep the travel lane open for vehicles.
• Trim tree branches that hang over the driveway to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure mowed or cut short, particularly where open green space meets shrub or brush areas.
• Thin or remove shrubs clustered near any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Cut back brush encroaching on the driveway entrance from the road to keep the entry point clearly visible and accessible.
• Separate shrub groupings near the house by removing some plants to create gaps between them.
• Keep the single driveway free of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and debris along its full length so it remains passable at all times.
